answer.held_back_by: Probably the politics door never opening. I stayed honest and did the work well, but STAND stayed low at 35ish, so I was a safe pair of hands nobody famous noticed. Being boring and clean has a ceiling.
answer.ending_fair_why: I reached the top of the service with a clean record and I chose that path myself. The line about no street named after you fits. I'm a bit sore that the politics offer never came, but the game did hint it was rumour only.
answer.chase_next: The politics ending. I'd play more of the grassroots stuff, say yes to the hint in Year 15 and see if I get invited in, because that's the Minister Salary fantasy and I never saw it.
answer.play_again_why: It was 38 years of taps and the middle was a long flat stretch. Maybe later with a different plan, but not tonight.
answer.title_fit_why: My run was about slow, steady years in the service, appraisals and being trusted, not about pay or becoming a minister. Minister Salary is the catchier name but it didn't match what I played.

DARREN LIM · THE FINAL POSITION
Permanent Secretary

The top of the civil service. No street is named after you and none ever will be, which is rather the point.

RETIRED AS Permanent Secretary
AT AGE 65
LIFETIME EARNINGS $25.55M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Senior Director. You were not told.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 27, in The Counter, you chose "Tell them exactly why it will fail." It raised your ceiling to Permanent Secretary, the top of the service.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
